facts.content: Patient has a 6-week history of diffuse aches and fatigue with decreased energy.
facts.source_text: CC: 6-wk h/o diffuse aches and fatigue/↓energy

facts.content: Symptoms began about 2 weeks after returning from a US holiday in late January/early February.
facts.source_text: Onset ~2 wks after return from US holiday (end Jan/early Feb)

facts.content: The patient was active hiking in shorts and boots during the US holiday with no known tick bite.
facts.source_text: active hiking in shorts/boots; no known tick bite

facts.content: Patient reports decreased appetite, but weight is stable.
Patient reports decreased exercise and is attending work but is less effective.
facts.source_text: exercise ↓; attending work but less effective

facts.content: Patient had a rash on the posterior calf in mid to late February with minimal itch, which resolved over about 2 weeks.
facts.source_text: Rash: posterior calf lesion mid–late Feb, minimal itch, resolved over ~2 wks

facts.content: Patient had a sore throat and possible fever around the time of the rash.
facts.source_text: had sore throat around that time ± fever

facts.content: No persistent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms.
No cough, shortness of breath, or phlegm.
No dysphagia, heartburn, or abdominal pain.
No diarrhea, vomiting, or blood in the stool.
No urinary symptoms.
No focal neurological symptoms.
No joint swelling.
Occasional headache with malaise.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient has a history of hay fever.
Patient uses a daily preventer inhaler.
Patient uses an over-the-counter antihistamine.
Patient works in health tech and lives with his wife.
facts.source_text: works in health tech; lives w/ wife

facts.content: Patient consumes alcohol occasionally.
Patient has subacute fatigue with generalized myalgias/arthralgias for about 6 weeks post-travel and a transient calf rash in mid to late February.
facts.source_text: Subacute fatigue with generalized myalgias/arthralgias x ~6 wks post-travel; transient calf rash mid–late Feb.

facts.content: Consideration of Lyme disease and other causes of fatigue is advised.
facts.source_text: Consider Lyme disease; other causes of fatigue also possible.

facts.content: Plan to conduct blood tests including FBC, U&E, LFT, and Lyme serology.
facts.source_text: Blood tests: FBC, U&E, LFT; Lyme serology

facts.content: If Lyme serology is positive, start appropriate antibiotics.
facts.source_text: If Lyme serology +: start appropriate antibiotics

facts.content: Book blood draw via support line and arrange telephone follow-up in about 1 week after results.
